questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel engaged in dredging is a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel aground is a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel engaged in mine clearance is a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel constrained by her draught is a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel engaged in dredging, surveying or underwater operations is a vessel restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel engaged in mine clearance operations is not defined as restricted in her ability to manoeuvre.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel not under command is a vessel that has chosen to stop its engine.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel not under command is a vessel that has stopped its engine but the engine is still available for use.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A vessel not under command means a vessel which from the nature of her work is restricted in her ability to manoeuvre as required by the Rules and is therefore unable to keep out of the way of another vessel.

questions.subject: Collision Regulations (COLREG)
questions.question: A sailing vessel means any vessel under sail provided that propelling machinery, if fitted, is not being used.
